chapter: Virginia school and first Washington bands
title: Missing royalties and his friendship with Mundy
summary: His name was added later, after missing the first royalties; he says Billie Holiday's book reports $75 each, and he held no grudge against his friend.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Well, when did you finally get your name on the record?

Oh, well, I missed all of the royalties from the first record because my name wasn't on it then and -- from the first months of that Billie Holiday record. And that was the most lucrative part of it, you know. I got it all later, about a year or so later.
Because I know in her book she says that you each got $75.00.
And that neither one of you ever saw Levit. another thing.

No, we didn't. And this -- when her book came out I hadn't gotten anything else from it at that time. But, you know, it was -- I felt bad about it because, you know, if somebody do that to do and you don't know him, you don't feel so bad. But for a friend, you know, a guy that you consider a friend -- because I was his best man at his wedding, you know, when he married his first wife, Dorothy, you know.

In fact, when she died later -- years later, after all this problem happened, I went out -- myself and Louis Taylor, another trombone player, and we played a song with organ for -- at her funeral, you know. But you know, I couldn't hold it against her. She didn't do nothing to me, you know. But these things happen in this business, you know.
But you had been working with him though for so long.
Yeah, we were friends, but that's part of the business I guess, you know.
